paragraphs: Here's the lesson, friend: when God says move, you move. Elisha told this woman a famine was coming, and she did just as the man of God said (2 Kings 8:1-2). No snooze button, no "let me think about it." Nobody around her could see the famine yet, and she packed up anyway.

Now look at what she came home to. Seven years gone, and she goes to the king to appeal for her house and her land (2 Kings 8:3). And right then Gehazi is telling the king about the son Elisha restored to life, and in she walks (2 Kings 8:5). I'm not going to tell you God arranged that timing, because the text doesn't say it. But I will say this: the king's order was "Restore all that was hers, along with all the proceeds of the field from the day that she left the country until now" (2 Kings 8:6).

So what does that mean for you, baker? Obeying God's word is never wasted, even when it costs you something and the payoff takes years. This woman gave up her home for seven years, and the king gave back everything, even the harvests she missed. Keep listening, keep going, and keep those ovens ready.
